parsed.attack: Huxe [52] is in the file and its cause is not dissolved by the defence offered: it closed the day after a platform shipped a near-identical personal-briefing feature, and the claim that a plot's own multi-season record cannot be copied overnight only holds once that record exists. For the first two seasons a new subscriber's Sunday briefing is a generic planting calendar, which the RHS, Gardeners' World and Gardenate already give away free - so the product is most copyable exactly when it is most vulnerable. Artifact [54] supplies the second cause, a product a core group loved that shut because "the market opportunity isn't big enough": there are roughly 330,000 allotment plots in the UK, a UK allotment briefing is close to worthless from November to February, and the first kill criterion - four consecutive Sunday opens - has to clear a four-month dead season every single year.
parsed.strongest_defence: The cold start is covered by the notebook the grower already keeps in the shed, which can be photographed and read in on the first evening, so the personal record exists from week one rather than season three, and allotment associations with existing newsletters are a channel no general platform bothers to work.
parsed.verdict_reason: Cheap long context genuinely dissolves the cost of preparing the briefing, but Huxe's commoditisation cause bites hardest in year one, before the personal record that is meant to prevent it has accumulated.
